This HTML Quarto file contains all the code used for the study titled "The impact of the two-child benefit cap on parental health in the UK: a triangulation of policy evaluation methods". This is Version 2, which is available as a preprint on MedrXiv (https://www.medrxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.03.30.26349774v2). 

This code is still divided into four sections: sections 1 and 2 deal with merging and data prep for code from Waves 1-15 (2009-2025) of UK Household Longitudinal Survey data, while section 3 is related to imputation, and section 4 is the analysis section.

# Section 1: merging USOC data files

This section of the code retrieves variables from multiple code files and creates a dataset that will then be edited/prepared in Section 2-3 and analysed in Section 4.

## Housekeeping code

I first start by installing and loading packages, then clearing all old objects if present. The working directory is not set because this runs inside an `.Rproj` file, but I do set a directory for data retrieval using the folder inside the file.

```{r}
#| label: install-packages
#| code-summary: Installing and loading packages needed

file.exists(".RData")

# installing and loading package(s) needed
install.packages("tidyverse") # data management
install.packages("data.table") # data management - specifically for larger dataset
install.packages("mice") # for multiple imputation
install.packages("MatchIt") # matching algorithm
install.packages("MatchThem") # matching with multiple imputation
install.packages("fixest") # running models
install.packages("openxlsx") # creating Excel files with output results
install.packages("patchwork") # for creating multipanel figures
install.packages("corrplot") # creating correlation plot
install.packages("cowplot") # for creating multipanel figures
install.packages("survey") # for weighted models
library(data.table) # load first because this code uses tidyverse more
library(MatchIt)        
library(MatchThem)      
library(fixest)         
library(openxlsx)       
library(patchwork)
library(corrplot)
library(cowplot)
library(survey)
library(mice)    
library(tidyverse)      # load LAST - masks many functions but you want its versions
```

```{r}
#| label: clean
#| code-summary: Clearing old objects if present

# clearing all old objects if present
rm(list = ls())
```

```{r}
#| label: set-paths
#| code-summary: Setting relevant paths
# not setting wd because I am working in an .Rproj file

# setting directory for data retrieval from folder in .Rproj file
ukhls <- "UKDA-6614-tab/tab/ukhls" 

# naming file produced at the end of this (change as updated)
outputfilename <- "20260812_UKHLS_total"

# setting "allWaves", which will be called below
allWaves <- letters[1:15]  # waves a-o, corresponding to waves 1-15 of UKHLS
```

```{r}
#| label: flow-counter
#| code-summary: Helper for recording sample sizes at each restriction
# each restriction step appends a row here, so the numbers for the sample flowchart are produced by the pipeline itself rather than reconstructed afterwards
sample_flow <- tibble(
  step          = character(),
  n_obs         = integer(),
  n_individuals = integer(),
  n_households  = integer()
)

record_flow <- function(data, label) {
  sample_flow <<- bind_rows(sample_flow, tibble(
    step          = label,
    n_obs         = nrow(data),
    n_individuals = n_distinct(data$pidp),
    n_households  = n_distinct(data$hidp)
  ))
  data
}
```

## Retrieving variables

Where possible, I am retrieving variables ending in `_dv`, as those have been derived from one or more sources in UKHLS and are therefore (possibly) more accurate.

### Household-level variables (`hhresp`)

List of variables retrieved from this file:

`hidp` - household ID

`fihhmnnet1_dv` - total net household income (no deductions), derived net monthly

`ieqmoecd_dv` - modified OECD equivalence scale

`agechy_dv` - age of youngest child, derived

```{r}
#| label: hhvars
#| code-summary: Retrieving variables from the household-level response files
# retrieving variables from "hhresp".tab - household-level response file
hhvars <- c("hidp", "fihhmnnet1_dv", "ieqmoecd_dv", "agechy_dv")
```

### Individual adult response variables (`indresp`, age 16+)

Note: I would have included `ukborn`, but it was a proxy variable, so I'll be retrieving it during the data cleaning step from the `xwavedat` file.

The original version of this code had included `disdif`(1-12) and `oprlg1`, variables for long-standing health, disability and religion, but due to high missingness, these variables had been excluded from analysis. As such, I've excluded them from data retrieval in this updated version.

List of variables retrieved from this file:

`pidp` - person ID

`hidp` - household ID

`intdaty_dv` - interview date year, derived

`intdatm_dv` - interview date month, derived

`ioutcome` - interview outcome (for filtering to productive interviews)

`ivfio` - interview type (to filter out proxies)

`ethn_dv` - ethnicity, derived (note that I would have included `ukborn` here, but it was a proxy variable, so I'll be retrieving it during the data cleaning step from xwavedat file)

`scghq`(a-l) - GHQ question variables

`sf1` - Wave 1 self-rated health measure

`scsf`(1-7) - SF-12 measures

`hiqual_dv` - highest educational qualification ever reported

`jbnssec3_dv` - current NS-SEC occupation class, derived (3 class version)

`mastat_dv` - de facto marital status, derived

`hcond`(1-16, 18-19, 21, 23-24, 26-29) - health conditions

`sclfsat1` - health satisfaction outcome measure

`sclfsato` - overall life satisfaction outcome measure

`finnow` - current financial situation, subjective rating

`finfut` - future financial situation, subjective rating

`urban_dv` - urban vs rural identification, derived

`memorig` - sample origin (used to show specific subsample)

`indscus_xw` - cross-sectional adult self-completion weight, GPS and EMB samples (wave 1)

`indscub_xw` - cross-sectional adult self-completion weight, GPS, EMB and BHPS samples (waves 2-5)

`indscui_xw` - cross-sectional adult self-completion weight, GPS, EMB, BHPS and IEMB samples (waves 6-13)

`indscg2_xw` - cross-sectional adult self-completion weight, all samples including GPS2 (wave 14)

`inding2_xw` - cross-sectional adult main interview weight, all samples including GPS2 (wave 15, where the self-completion distinction no longer applies)

`psu` - person sampling unit

`strata` - sampling strata

NB for weights, the self-completion one is prioritised for use over the main interview one in waves where there is a difference (so for wave 15, only the inding2 one is present)

```{r}
#| label: indvars
#| code-summary: Retrieving variables from the individual adult-level response files
# retrieving variables from "indresp".tab - individual/adult response file (16+)
indvars <- c("pidp", "hidp", "intdaty_dv", "intdatm_dv", "ioutcome", "ivfio", "ethn_dv", "scghqa", "scghqb", "scghqc", "scghqd", "scghqe", "scghqf", "scghqg", "scghqh", "scghqi", "scghqj", "scghqk", "scghql", "sf1", "scsf1", "scsf2a", "scsf2b", "scsf3a", "scsf3b", "scsf4a", "scsf4b", "scsf5", "scsf6a", "scsf6b", "scsf6c", "scsf7", "hiqual_dv", "jbnssec3_dv", "mastat_dv", "hcond1", "hcond2", "hcond3", "hcond4", "hcond5", "hcond6", "hcond7", "hcond8", "hcond9", "hcond10", "hcond11", "hcond12",  "hcond13", "hcond14", "hcond15", "hcond16", "hcond18", "hcond19", "hcond21", "hcond23", "hcond24", "hcond26", "hcond27", "hcond28", "hcond29", "sclfsat1", "sclfsato", "finnow", "finfut", "urban_dv", "memorig", "indscus_xw", "indscub_xw", "indscui_xw", "indscg2_xw", "inding2_xw", "psu", "strata")
```

### Household enumeration variables (`indall`)

List of variables retrieved from this file:

`pidp` - person ID

`hidp` - household ID

`age_dv` - age in completed years at time of interview, derived

`sex_dv` - sex, derived

`doby_dv` - date of birth year, derived

```{r}
#| label: indallvars
#| code-summary: Retrieving variables from the household enumeration response files
# retrieving variables from "indall".tab - enumeration of all household members
indallvars <- c("pidp", "hidp", "age_dv", "sex_dv", "doby_dv")
```

## Merging variables: R-native approach

Now that I have the retrieved variables, this section reads all waves of each file type, then merges them, by reading a file from each wave and adding a wave indicator.

### Reading and appending files

```{r}
#| label: read-wave-file
#| code-summary: Reading wave files
# helper function to read a wave file and add wave indicator
read_wave_file <- function(wave, filename, vars_to_keep) {
  filepath <- file.path(ukhls, paste0(wave, "_", filename, ".tab"))
  if (!file.exists(filepath)) {
    warning("missing file: ", filepath)
    return(NULL)
  }
  # first read just column names to see what exists
  col_names <- names(read_tsv(filepath, n_max = 0, show_col_types = FALSE))
  # checking for both prefixed and non-prefixed versions of variables
  wave_vars <- paste0(wave, "_", vars_to_keep)  # e.g., "a_hidp"
  no_prefix_vars <- vars_to_keep  # e.g., "pidp"
  # keeping variables that exist (either with or without prefix)
  existing_vars <- c(wave_vars[wave_vars %in% col_names], 
                     no_prefix_vars[no_prefix_vars %in% col_names])
  if (length(existing_vars) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  # reading only those columns
  df <- read_tsv(filepath, col_select = all_of(existing_vars), show_col_types = FALSE)
  # removing wave prefix from variables that have it
  names(df) <- gsub(paste0("^", wave, "_"), "", names(df))
  # adding wave indicator
  df$wavename <- which(letters == wave)
  return(df)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: hhresp-append
#| code-summary: Reading and appending 'hhresp' files (household responses)
# reading and appending files, by type
# HHRESP files (household level)
hhresp_list <- map(allWaves, ~read_wave_file(.x, "hhresp", hhvars))
hhresp_all <- bind_rows(hhresp_list)
table(hhresp_all$wavename)  # expect 15 waves
```

```{r}
#| label: indresp-append
#| code-summary: Reading and appending 'indresp' files (adult responses)
# INDRESP files (adult responses)
indresp_list <- map(allWaves, ~read_wave_file(.x, "indresp", indvars))
indresp_all <- bind_rows(indresp_list)
table(indresp_all$wavename)  # expect 15 waves
```

```{r}
#| label: indresp-check
#| code-summary: Verifying the appended individual file against expected structure
# pidp should identify a person uniquely within a wave. if it does not, the joins below will silently expand rows
stopifnot(indresp_all %>% count(pidp, wavename) %>% filter(n > 1) %>% nrow() == 0)

# the cross-sectional weight variables are published per wave for the sample bases available at that wave, so each wave should carry exactly the expected columns and each should be complete. this table is the reference: a variable appearing outside its own block, or missing values inside it, means the append has gone wrong
indresp_all %>%
  group_by(wavename) %>%
  summarise(across(c(indscus_xw, indscub_xw, indscui_xw, indscg2_xw, inding2_xw),
                   ~sum(!is.na(.x))),
            n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  print(n = 15)

# and the same as a hard check on the weight actually used downstream
wave_weight_complete <- indresp_all %>%
  mutate(expected = case_when(
    wavename == 1 ~ indscus_xw,
    wavename %in% 2:5 ~ indscub_xw,
    wavename %in% 6:13 ~ indscui_xw,
    wavename == 14 ~ indscg2_xw,
    wavename == 15 ~ inding2_xw
  )) %>%
  summarise(missing = sum(is.na(expected))) %>%
  pull(missing)

stopifnot(wave_weight_complete == 0)
```

```{r}
#| label: merging-both
#| code-summary: Merging 'hhresp' and 'indresp'
# merging everything together
# starting with hhresp (household level)
df_final <- hhresp_all

# merging indresp by hidp and wavename
df_final <- df_final %>%
  left_join(indresp_all, by = c("hidp", "wavename"), suffix = c("_hh", ""))
```

```{r}
#| label: read-indall
#| code-summary: Reading and appending 'indall' files (all individuals, including children)
# INDALL files (all individuals - for household enumeration)
indall_list <- map(allWaves, ~read_wave_file(.x, "indall", indallvars))
indall_all <- bind_rows(indall_list)
table(indall_all$wavename)  # expect 15 waves
```

```{r}
#| label: merge-indall
#| code-summary: Merging 'indall' into main file
# merging indall to get all household members (including children)
df_final <- df_final %>%
  left_join(indall_all, by = c("hidp", "wavename", "pidp"), suffix = c("", "_indall"))
```

```{r}
#| label: merge-check
#| code-summary: Verifying that the merges did not duplicate or drop rows
# indall should identify a person uniquely within a wave, otherwise the join expands rows
stopifnot(indall_all %>% count(pidp, hidp, wavename) %>% filter(n > 1) %>% nrow() == 0)

# after both joins, a person should still appear once per wave. duplication here means one of the join keys was not unique in its source
stopifnot(
  df_final %>% filter(!is.na(pidp)) %>% count(pidp, hidp, wavename) %>% filter(n > 1) %>% nrow() == 0
)

# the merge should not create individual rows that were not in indresp
stopifnot(sum(!is.na(df_final$pidp)) <= nrow(indresp_all))

# individual records with no matching household questionnaire are dropped by the left join, since hhresp is the left-hand table. these people have no agechy_dv and so could not enter the analytic sample in any case, but the count is reported here because they leave the pipeline before the first flowchart step
indresp_all %>%
  anti_join(hhresp_all, by = c("hidp", "wavename")) %>%
  count(wavename) %>%
  print(n = 15)

nrow(indresp_all)
sum(!is.na(df_final$pidp))

# the weight block structure should be unchanged by the merge. if this differs from the table printed after indresp-append, the merge has altered values it should only have carried through
df_final %>%
  group_by(wavename) %>%
  summarise(across(c(indscus_xw, indscub_xw, indscui_xw, indscg2_xw, inding2_xw),
                   ~sum(!is.na(.x))),
            n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  print(n = 15)
```

### Cleaning merged files

I filter to productive interviews, specifically to narrow down the sample to interviews that happened, therefore which will have results.

```{r}
#| label: filter-productive
#| code-summary: Filter to productive interviews (excluding proxies)
df_final <- df_final %>%
  filter(ioutcome %in% c(11, 21)) %>%  # full productive and partial productive interviews
  filter(ivfio != 2 | is.na(ivfio)) %>%   # exclude proxy respondents
  record_flow("Productive, non-proxy interviews")
```

I then reorder columns for my own sake, to have the ID files at the beginning for viewing purposes, and save the resulting data frame.

```{r}
#| label: reorder-cols
#| code-summary: Reorder ID columns
# move pidp and hidp to the beginning of the file
UKHLS_total <- df_final %>% select(pidp, hidp, wavename, everything())
```

```{r}
#| label: source-verification
#| code-summary: Verifying the merged file against the raw wave files
# reads selected variables straight from the wave files and compares them against what UKHLS_total holds for the same people. this is the only check that does not depend on any object already in the environment, and so is the one that catches a merged file that has drifted out of step with its source
verify_wave <- function(wave_letter, wave_num, vars) {
  fp <- file.path(ukhls, paste0(wave_letter, "_indresp.tab"))
  raw <- read_tsv(fp,
                  col_select = all_of(c("pidp", paste0(wave_letter, "_", vars))),
                  show_col_types = FALSE)
  names(raw) <- gsub(paste0("^", wave_letter, "_"), "", names(raw))

  UKHLS_total %>%
    filter(wavename == wave_num) %>%
    select(pidp, all_of(vars)) %>%
    inner_join(raw, by = "pidp", suffix = c("_merged", "_source")) %>%
    summarise(
      wave = wave_num,
      n    = n(),
      across(ends_with("_merged"),
             ~sum(.x != get(sub("_merged$", "_source", cur_column())) |
                  is.na(.x) != is.na(get(sub("_merged$", "_source", cur_column()))),
                  na.rm = TRUE))
    )
}

check_vars <- c("scghqa", "sclfsato", "finnow", "hiqual_dv", "mastat_dv", "urban_dv")

# checked at the start, middle and end of the series, and at the two waves where the weight base changes
source_check <- bind_rows(
  verify_wave("a", 1,  check_vars),
  verify_wave("b", 2,  check_vars),
  verify_wave("c", 3,  check_vars),
  verify_wave("d", 4, check_vars),
  verify_wave("e", 5, check_vars),
  verify_wave("f", 6,  check_vars),
  verify_wave("g", 7,  check_vars),
  verify_wave("h", 8,  check_vars),
  verify_wave("i", 9,  check_vars),
  verify_wave("j", 10, check_vars),
  verify_wave("k", 11, check_vars),
  verify_wave("l", 12,  check_vars),
  verify_wave("m", 13,  check_vars),
  verify_wave("n", 14, check_vars),
  verify_wave("o", 15, check_vars)
)
source_check

# every count should be zero
stopifnot(source_check %>% select(-wave, -n) %>% sum() == 0)
```

In this case, I then save both the long file and the environment in case other files in the creation of the long file are needed.

```{r}
#| label: save-outputs
#| code-summary: Saving outputs
# saving the long file
saveRDS(UKHLS_total, paste0(outputfilename, ".rds"))

# indall_all is saved separately because section 2 needs it to build the child counts, and it is the only other section 1 object used downstream
saveRDS(indall_all, "20260812_indall_all.rds")

# the flow counter is saved so that the sample sizes recorded in section 1 carry through to the flowchart table produced at the end of section 3
saveRDS(sample_flow, "20260812_sample_flow.rds")

# removing extra duplicate lists
rm(hhresp_list, indresp_list, indall_list, df_final)
```

# Section 2: cleaning the USOC data file

The purpose of this to clean the USOC data file, merged above from Section 1.

It uses output from the above file as input, but there should also be an added environment saved from that file too. If the entire environment is needed (which it is if you haven't run the merge code before this), load the below code.

```{r}
#| label: load-environment
#| code-summary: Loading section 1 outputs
# section 2 needs UKHLS_total, indall_all, the running flow counter, the ukhls path, and the record_flow helper. these are loaded from saved files and recreated here rather than restored from a workspace image, so that only the objects the pipeline actually produced are brought in and a stale object cannot be carried across
rm(list = ls())

ukhls <- "UKDA-6614-tab/tab/ukhls"
UKHLS_total <- readRDS("20260812_UKHLS_total.rds")
indall_all  <- readRDS("20260812_indall_all.rds")
sample_flow <- readRDS("20260812_sample_flow.rds")

record_flow <- function(data, label) {
  sample_flow <<- bind_rows(sample_flow, tibble(
    step          = label,
    n_obs         = nrow(data),
    n_individuals = n_distinct(data$pidp),
    n_households  = n_distinct(data$hidp)
  ))
  data
}
```

The sample selection criteria will include individuals with at least one child 5 or under and at least one outcome response.

## Time and linking structures

First, I inspect the interview years for missingness and checking Ns of those.

```{r}
#| label: time-inspect
#| code-summary: Checking interview year
table(UKHLS_total$intdaty_dv, useNA = "ifany")
table(UKHLS_total$intdatm_dv, useNA = "ifany")
```

Then, I build clean time variables (`intyear`, `intmonth`).

Some things I am doing while building these variables:

- Renaming `intdaty_dv` to `intyear` for ease, and selecting relevant anchoring variables: `pidp` (person ID), `hidp` (household ID), `wavename` (even though we will be using year for analysis, having the wavename increases consistency for linking), and `intyear`.

```{r}
#| label: time-clean
#| code-summary: Building clean time variables ('intyear', 'intmonth')
UKHLS_clean <- UKHLS_total %>%
  rename(intyear = intdaty_dv) %>%
  rename(intmonth = intdatm_dv) %>%
  mutate(intyear = case_when(
    intyear == -9 ~ NA_real_,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(intyear)
  )) %>%
  filter(!is.na(intyear)) %>%
  mutate(intmonth = case_when(
    intmonth == -9 ~ NA_real_, # missing
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(intmonth)
  )) %>%
  select(pidp, hidp, wavename, intmonth, intyear) %>%
  record_flow("Valid interview year")
```

```{r}
#| label: time-check
#| code-summary: Sense-checking time variable missingness
# sense-checking intyear, intmonth, and wavename vars before proceeding
table(UKHLS_clean$intyear, useNA = "ifany")
table(UKHLS_clean$intmonth, useNA = "ifany")
table(UKHLS_clean$wavename, UKHLS_clean$intyear, useNA = "ifany")
```

## Exposure variables

This section creates the family variables, identifying parents and children, as well as creating exposure variables. I first start by retrieving `indall` files as needed to get all household members (including children); these should already be loaded but if not, go back and load the entire environment.

From this, I then obtain values on the number of children under 18, number of children aged 5 or under, a youngest child year-of-birth variable, and a flag on if any third-or-more-children are born in 2017 (this flag will be removed later after the imputation step.)

```{r}
#| label: child-info
#| code-summary: Identifying child counts and cap-relevant birth timing
child_info <- indall_all %>%
  filter(age_dv >= 0 & age_dv < 18) %>%
  mutate(doby_dv = if_else(doby_dv < 0, NA_real_, as.numeric(doby_dv))) %>%
  group_by(hidp, wavename) %>%
  summarise(
    n_children_u18     = n(), # number of children under 18
    n_children_5_under = sum(age_dv <= 5), # number of children aged 5 or under
    youngest_child_yob = if (all(is.na(doby_dv))) NA_real_ else max(doby_dv, na.rm = TRUE),
    # drop the two oldest children, then look for a 2017 birth among the rest
    any_third_plus_2017 = as.numeric(any(sort(doby_dv)[-(1:2)] == 2017)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

Finally, I merge the information on children and filter the clean dataset to households with valid age data and at least one child ≤5.

```{r}
#| label: merge-child-info
#| code-summary: Merging child info and age of youngest child into clean dataset
UKHLS_clean <- UKHLS_clean %>%
  left_join(child_info, by = c("hidp", "wavename")) %>%
  left_join(
    UKHLS_total %>% select(pidp, hidp, wavename, age_youngest_child = agechy_dv),
    by = c("pidp", "hidp", "wavename")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # replace NAs with 0 for households with no children under 18
    n_children_u18      = replace_na(n_children_u18, 0),
    n_children_5_under  = replace_na(n_children_5_under, 0),
    any_third_plus_2017 = replace_na(any_third_plus_2017, 0),
    # recode missing codes to NA, consistent with all other variables
    age_youngest_child = case_when(
      age_youngest_child < 0 ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ as.numeric(age_youngest_child)
    )
  )

# Restricting clean dataset to analytic sample
UKHLS_analytic <- UKHLS_clean %>%
  filter(n_children_5_under > 0 & !is.na(age_youngest_child)) %>%
  record_flow("At least one child aged 5 or under")
```

I use information created from steps above to construct variables which will be used for analyses below, including:

- `family_3plus` - binary indicator of whether someone has three or more children

- `post_policy_month` - policy timing indicator

- `treated` - used to distinguish 1-2 children individuals specifically from 3+ children individuals *affected by the policy* (distinct from unaffected 3+ children individuals)

- `time_since_policy` - a centered year variable (where April 2017 = 0)

```{r}
#| label: treatment-vars
#| code-summary: Creating exposure and treatment variables
UKHLS_analytic <- UKHLS_analytic %>%
  mutate(
    # family structure indicator
    family_3plus = ifelse(n_children_u18 >= 3, 1, 0),
    
    # policy timing indicator (April 2017 cutoff)
    post_policy_month = ifelse(intyear > 2017 | (intyear == 2017 & intmonth >= 4), 1, 0),
    
    # treatment group assignment (time-invariant)
    # all rows have a child aged 5 or under by construction of the analytic sample
    # 0 = control (1-2 children)
    # 1 = treated (3+ children, youngest child born 2017+)
    # NA = excluded (unaffected 3+)
    treated = case_when(
      family_3plus == 0 ~ 0,
      family_3plus == 1 & youngest_child_yob >= 2017 ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    
    # time variable centered at policy implementation in April 2017
    time_since_policy = (intyear - 2017) + (intmonth - 4) / 12)
```

## Outcome variables

For ease of interpretation, all directionality of coding will be kept consistent between variables (so higher scores = worse outcomes). Outcomes created are in three groups - **mental health** (psychological distress, life satisfaction), **general health** (HRQoL, self-rated health, health satisfaction), and **financial health** (financial situation and financial outlook). I will note that, for consistency's sake, the labels use the old nomenclature within the code, but you can use the different headings as indication of the outcomes or refer to the specific list below:

**Mental health**

- psychological distress: `GHQ_total`

- life satisfaction: `life_sat`

**General health**

- health-related quality of life (HRQoL): `SF_total`

- self-rated health: `self_health`

- health satisfaction: `health_sat`

**Financial health**

- financial situation: `finnow`

- financial outlook: `finfut`

The first step is filtering the outcomes to clean them. To this end, I will only be including observations where at least one outcome has a response (and imputing other responses if missing).

```{r}
#| label: outcomes-init
#| code-summary: Retrieving outcome variables
outcomes <- UKHLS_total %>%
  select(pidp, hidp, wavename,
         all_of(c("scghqa","scghqb","scghqc","scghqd","scghqe","scghqf",
                  "scghqg","scghqh","scghqi","scghqj","scghqk","scghql")),
         sf1,
         all_of(c("scsf1","scsf2a","scsf2b","scsf3a","scsf3b","scsf4a",
                  "scsf4b","scsf5","scsf6a","scsf6b","scsf6c","scsf7")),
         sclfsat1, sclfsato, finnow, finfut)
```

The way this had initially been done, I retrieved the outcomes based on where they appeared in the USOC dataset, so I am cleaning each outcome separately.

### Psychological distress (`GHQ_total`)

This measure uses GHQ-12 coding questionnaire data. First, I am checking values of each GHQ question before changing.

```{r}
#| label: ghq-inspect
#| code-summary: Checking GHQ-12 variable frequencies
# scghqa - concentration
table(outcomes$scghqa, useNA = "ifany") 
# scghqb - loss of sleep
table(outcomes$scghqb, useNA = "ifany") 
# scghqc - playing a useful role
table(outcomes$scghqc, useNA = "ifany") 
# scghqd - capable of making decisions
table(outcomes$scghqd, useNA = "ifany") 
# scghqe - constantly under strain
table(outcomes$scghqe, useNA = "ifany") 
# scghqf - problem overcoming difficulties
table(outcomes$scghqf, useNA = "ifany") 
# scghqg - enjoying day-to-day activities
table(outcomes$scghqg, useNA = "ifany") 
# scghqh - ability to face up to problems
table(outcomes$scghqh, useNA = "ifany") 
# scghqi - unhappy or depressed
table(outcomes$scghqi, useNA = "ifany") 
# scghqj - losing confidence
table(outcomes$scghqj, useNA = "ifany") 
# scghqk - believing worthless
table(outcomes$scghqk, useNA = "ifany") 
# scghql - general happiness
table(outcomes$scghql, useNA = "ifany") 
```

Now I am renaming the dataset variable names for ease of use.

```{r}
#| label: ghq-rename
#| code-summary: Renaming GHQ variables
# now cleaning dataset variables - renaming first for ease of use
outcomes <- outcomes %>%
  rename(GHQ_q1 = scghqa,
         GHQ_q2 = scghqb,
         GHQ_q3 = scghqc,
         GHQ_q4 = scghqd,
         GHQ_q5 = scghqe,
         GHQ_q6 = scghqf,
         GHQ_q7 = scghqg,
         GHQ_q8 = scghqh,
         GHQ_q9 = scghqi,
         GHQ_q10 = scghqj,
         GHQ_q11 = scghqk,
         GHQ_q12 = scghql)
```

Now, is the recoding: updating each question and scoring `-1` (don't know), `-2` (refused), `-7` (proxy), `-8` (not applicable) and `-9` (missing) to NA. All measures are considered "recently" in terms of time frame.

```{r}
#| label: ghq-recode
#| code-summary: Recoding GHQ variables
outcomes <- outcomes %>%
  mutate(across(GHQ_q1:GHQ_q12, ~case_when(
    .x %in% c(-9, -8, -7, -2, -1) ~ NA_real_,
    .x == 1 ~ 0,
    .x == 2 ~ 1,
    .x == 3 ~ 2,
    .x == 4 ~ 3,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(.x)
  )))
```

Finally, I run person-mean imputation in order to substitute missingness of individual items (since those tend to be MNAR - missing not at random - and we didn't want to exclude people who might have systematically chosen not to answer certain questions) for the measurements, and then created a total GHQ measure (0–36) and ran a sense check on the distribution of values.

```{r}
#| label: ghq-total
#| code-summary: Person-mean imputation
# person-mean imputation
outcomes <- outcomes %>%
  mutate(
    # calculate person mean across all GHQ items
    person_mean = rowMeans(select(., GHQ_q1:GHQ_q12), na.rm = TRUE),
    # impute missing values with person mean
    across(GHQ_q1:GHQ_q12, ~if_else(is.na(.x), person_mean, .x)),
    # create composite score
    GHQ_total = if_else(is.nan(person_mean), NA_real_, rowSums(across(GHQ_q1:GHQ_q12)))
  ) %>%
  select(-person_mean)
# checking GHQ total distribution
table(outcomes$GHQ_total, useNA = "ifany")
```

### Health-related quality of life (`SF_total`) and self-rated health (`self_health`)

For this measure, I used the composite score of the SF-12 (self-rated health will be the first question, which I will explain that in a bit). Similarly to above, I created a score by cleaning and adding each question's measure.

For SF-12, it doesn't seem like measurements from separate questions are available for wave 1, so I will have to keep that in mind. I first check these separate measures.

```{r}
#| label: sf12-inspect
#| code-summary: Checking SF-12 variable frequencies
# scsf1 - question 1 - also general health question
table(outcomes$sf1, useNA = "ifany")
table(outcomes$scsf1, useNA = "ifany")
# scsf2a - health limiting moderate activities
table(outcomes$scsf2a, useNA = "ifany")
# scsf2b - health limiting climbing several flights of stairs
table(outcomes$scsf2b, useNA = "ifany")
# scsf3a - physical health limits amount of work
table(outcomes$scsf3a, useNA = "ifany")
# scsf3b - physical health limits type of work
table(outcomes$scsf3b, useNA = "ifany")
# scsf4a - mental health meant accomplished less
table(outcomes$scsf4a, useNA = "ifany")
# scsf4b - mental health meant worked less carefully
table(outcomes$scsf4b, useNA = "ifany")
# scsf5 - pain interfered with work
table(outcomes$scsf5, useNA = "ifany")
# scsf6a - feeling calm and peaceful
table(outcomes$scsf6a, useNA = "ifany")
# scsf6b - had a lot of energy
table(outcomes$scsf6b, useNA = "ifany")
# scsf6c - felt downhearted and depressed
table(outcomes$scsf6c, useNA = "ifany")
# scsf7 - physical or mental health interfered with social life
table(outcomes$scsf7, useNA = "ifany")
```

I needed to add this because the SF-12 is scored differently directionally for certain items.

The SF-12 is scored from 1–5, with some higher scores initially indicating better health, but now will be scored for higher scores to indicate worse health). Updating each question — numbers will be reverse-coded, but scoring `-1` (don't know), `-2` (refused), `-7` (proxy), `-8` (not applicable), `-9` (missing) and `-10` (not available for IEMB) to NA. All measures "recently" in terms of time frame.

To reverse-score (higher was better, need to flip):

- Out of 5: 3a, 3b, 4a, 4b, 6c, 7
- Out of 3: 2a, 2b

To keep same score (higher already = worse):

- Out of 5: 1, 5, 6a, 6b

**Self-rated health** (`self_health`)

To create this measure, I specifically combined `sf1` (Wave 1) and `scsf1` (Wave 2+) responses for question 1 of the SF-12. This was done because, from wave 2 onwards, scsf provides the individual-level responses to SF-12 questions, while sf1 becomes a proxy measure. That being said, the specific naming of the variable happens below in the final outcomes cleaning step.

```{r}
#| label: sf12-self-rated-health
#| code-summary: Creating combined self-rated health variable ('sf1' from Wave 1, 'scsf1' from Wave 2+)
outcomes <- outcomes %>%
  mutate(
    # cleaning both variables - KEEP
    sf1_clean = case_when(
      sf1 %in% c(-10, -9, -8, -7, -2, -1) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ as.numeric(sf1)
    ),
    scsf1_clean = case_when(
      scsf1 %in% c(-10, -9, -8, -7, -2, -1) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ as.numeric(scsf1)
    ),
    # combine: using sf1 ONLY for Wave 1, scsf1 for all other waves
    scsf1_combined = case_when(
      wavename == 1 ~ sf1_clean,  # Wave 1 only
      TRUE ~ scsf1_clean  # Wave 2+ use scsf1
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-sf1_clean, -scsf1_clean) # scsf1_combined in SF-12 calculation
```

```{r}
#| label: sf12-recode
#| code-summary: Cleaning and reverse-coding remaining SF-12 items
outcomes <- outcomes %>%
  mutate(
    # 2a, 2b: REVERSE CODE (1=limited a lot is worse, but coded as 1, need to flip to 3)
    # Original: 1=limited a lot (worst), 3=not limited (best)
    # Want: 3=limited a lot (worst), 1=not limited (best)
    scsf2a = case_when(
      scsf2a %in% c(-10, -9, -8, -7, -2, -1) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ 4 - as.numeric(scsf2a)  # reverse for 1-3 scale
    ),
    scsf2b = case_when(
      scsf2b %in% c(-10, -9, -8, -7, -2, -1) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ 4 - as.numeric(scsf2b)  # reverse for 1-3 scale
    ),
    
    # 3a, 3b: REVERSE CODE (1=all the time is worst, need to flip)
    # Original: 1=all the time (worst), 5=none of the time (best)
    # Want: 5=all the time (worst), 1=none of the time (best)
    scsf3a = case_when(
      scsf3a %in% c(-10, -9, -8, -7, -2, -1) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ 6 - as.numeric(scsf3a)  # reverse-coding
    ),
    scsf3b = case_when(
      scsf3b %in% c(-10, -9, -8, -7, -2, -1) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ 6 - as.numeric(scsf3b)  # reverse-coding
    ),
    
    # 4a, 4b: REVERSE CODE (1=all the time is worst, need to flip)
    scsf4a = case_when(
      scsf4a %in% c(-10, -9, -8, -7, -2, -1) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ 6 - as.numeric(scsf4a)  # reverse-coding
    ),
    scsf4b = case_when(
      scsf4b %in% c(-10, -9, -8, -7, -2, -1) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ 6 - as.numeric(scsf4b)  # reverse-coding
    ),
    
    # 5: KEEP SAME (1=not at all is best, 5=extremely is worst) - already correct direction
    scsf5 = case_when(
      scsf5 %in% c(-10, -9, -8, -7, -2, -1) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ as.numeric(scsf5)  # NO reverse-coding
    ),
    
    # 6a: KEEP SAME (1=all the time calm is best, 5=none of the time calm is worst) - already correct direction
    scsf6a = case_when(
      scsf6a %in% c(-10, -9, -8, -7, -2, -1) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ as.numeric(scsf6a)  # NO reverse-coding
    ),
    
    # 6b: KEEP SAME (1=all the time energy is best, 5=none of the time energy is worst) - already correct direction
    scsf6b = case_when(
      scsf6b %in% c(-10, -9, -8, -7, -2, -1) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ as.numeric(scsf6b)  # NO reverse-coding
    ),
    
    # 6c: REVERSE CODE (1=all the time depressed is worst, need to flip)
    # Original: 1=all the time (worst), 5=none of the time (best)
    # Want: 5=all the time (worst), 1=none of the time (best)
    scsf6c = case_when(
      scsf6c %in% c(-10, -9, -8, -7, -2, -1) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ 6 - as.numeric(scsf6c)  # reverse-coding
    ),
    
    # 7: REVERSE CODE (1=all the time interfered is worst, need to flip)
    # Original: 1=all the time (worst), 5=none of the time (best)
    # Want: 5=all the time (worst), 1=none of the time (best)
    scsf7 = case_when(
      scsf7 %in% c(-10, -9, -8, -7, -2, -1) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ 6 - as.numeric(scsf7)  # reverse-coding
    )
  )
```

Similar to the psychological distress outcome above, since this is from a questionnaire, we didn't want to exclude individuals because of selective non-responses, so we used the same approach here for person-mean-imputing missing values before creating the total `SF_total` variable and doing a sense check on the distribution.

```{r}
#| label: sf-12-imp-gen
#| code-summary: Person-mean imputation and generation of 'SF_total'
# person-mean imputation step for SF-12 
outcomes <- outcomes %>%
  mutate(
    # items sit on two scales (1-5 and 1-3), so the person mean is taken over
    # proportion-of-range and mapped back onto each item's own scale
    prop_mean = rowMeans(
      cbind(
        (select(., scsf1_combined, scsf3a, scsf3b, scsf4a, scsf4b,
                scsf5, scsf6a, scsf6b, scsf6c, scsf7) - 1) / 4,
        (select(., scsf2a, scsf2b) - 1) / 2
      ),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    # impute missing values
    across(c(scsf1_combined, scsf3a, scsf3b, scsf4a, scsf4b,
             scsf5, scsf6a, scsf6b, scsf6c, scsf7),
           ~if_else(is.na(.x), 1 + prop_mean * 4, .x)),
    across(c(scsf2a, scsf2b),
           ~if_else(is.na(.x), 1 + prop_mean * 2, .x)),
    # create SF total
    SF_total = if_else(is.nan(prop_mean), NA_real_,
                       rowSums(across(c(scsf1_combined, scsf2a, scsf2b, scsf3a, scsf3b,
                                        scsf4a, scsf4b, scsf5, scsf6a, scsf6b, scsf6c, scsf7))))
  ) %>%
  select(-prop_mean)
```

```{r}
#| label: sf12-check
#| code-summary: Checking SF total distribution
table(outcomes$SF_total, useNA = "ifany") 
```

### Health satisfaction (`health_sat`)

I then code the health satisfaction variable, with the scale being 1–7, and `1` initially being "completely dissatisfied" and `7` being "completely satisfied". Now switching to `1` = "completely satisfied" and `7` = "completely dissatisfied". Setting `-1` (don't know), `-2` (refused), `-7` (proxy), `-8` (not applicable), `-9` (missing), `-10` (not available for IEMB) to `NA`.

```{r}
#| label: health-sat
#| code-summary: Coding health satifaction variable
table(outcomes$sclfsat1, useNA = "ifany")
outcomes <- outcomes %>%
  rename(health_sat = sclfsat1) %>%
  mutate(health_sat = case_when(
    health_sat %in% c(-10, -9, -8, -7, -2, -1) ~ NA_real_,
    TRUE ~ 8 - as.numeric(health_sat)) # reverse-coding
  )
table(outcomes$health_sat, useNA = "ifany")
```

### Life satisfaction (`life_sat`)

I then code the life satisfaction variable, once again, with a 1–7 scale, with `1` initially being "completely dissatisfied" and `7` being "completely satisfied", and switching to `1` = "completely satisfied" and `7` = "completely dissatisfied". Same `NA`-coding rules as health satisfaction.

```{r}
#| label: life-sat
#| code-summary: Coding life satifaction variable
table(outcomes$sclfsato, useNA = "ifany")
# first, checking values of LS measure before changing
outcomes <- outcomes %>%
  rename(life_sat = sclfsato) %>%
  mutate(life_sat = case_when(
    life_sat %in% c(-10, -9, -8, -7, -2, -1) ~ NA_real_,
    TRUE ~ 8 - as.numeric(life_sat))) # reverse-coding
table(outcomes$life_sat, useNA = "ifany")
```

### Financial situation (`finnow`)

This question asks individuals to rate their *current* subjective financial situation, which we are referring to as "financial situation".

This is rated on a scale of 1–5, with `1` being "living comfortably" and `5` being "finding it very difficult".

```{r}
#| label: finnow
#| code-summary: Coding financial situation variable
table(outcomes$finnow, useNA = "ifany")
outcomes <- outcomes %>%
  mutate(finnow = case_when(
    finnow %in% c(-9, -8, -7, -2, -1) ~ NA_real_,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(finnow)
  ))
table(outcomes$finnow, useNA = "ifany")
```

### Financial outlook (`finfut`)

This question asks individuals to rate their *future* subjective financial situation a year from now, which we are referring to as "financial outlook".

The original scale does 1–3, with `1` being "better off" and `2` being "worse off" and `3` being about the same. I am changing it to a rating where `1` is still "better off", but it is incrementally worse, so `2` = "about the same" and `3` = "worse off".

```{r}
#| label: finfut
#| code-summary: Coding financial outlook variable
table(outcomes$finfut, useNA = "ifany")
outcomes <- outcomes %>%
  mutate(finfut = case_when(
    finfut %in% c(-9, -8, -7, -2, -1) ~ NA_real_,
    finfut == 1 ~ 1,
    finfut == 2 ~ 3,
    finfut == 3 ~ 2,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(finfut)
  ))
table(outcomes$finfut, useNA = "ifany") 
```

### Simplifying outcome dataset and merging back into analytic sample

After all the outcomes have been cleaned and created, I want to simplify the outcome dataset to just the cleaned variables needed, but keeping original `outcomes` df if needed. Also, this step renames the self-rated health question from `scsf1_combined`, which was created above.

When adding back in, I am only adding back in observations that have at least one outcome measure.

```{r}
#| label: outcomes-clean
#| code-summary: Cleaning and merging outcomes
outcomes_clean <- outcomes %>%
  rename(self_health = scsf1_combined) %>%
  filter(if_any(c(GHQ_total, SF_total, self_health, health_sat,
                  life_sat, finnow, finfut), ~ !is.na(.x))) %>%
  select(pidp, hidp, wavename, GHQ_total, SF_total, self_health, health_sat, life_sat, finnow, finfut)
  
# adding cleaned vars back in
UKHLS_analytic <- UKHLS_analytic %>%
  inner_join(outcomes_clean, by = c("pidp", "hidp", "wavename")) %>%
  record_flow("At least one outcome response")
```

## Sociodemographic variables

The variables I am going to clean here are as follows: age, sex, year of birth, ethnicity, UK birth status, urbanicity, highest education level, and de-facto marital status.

- Age: `age_dv` from `indall` -\> `age` (time-varying)
- Sex: `sex_dv` from `indall` -\> `sex` (time-invariant)
- Year of birth: `doby_dv` from `indall` (time-varying)
- Ethnicity: `ethn_dv` from `indresp` -\> `ethn` & `ethn_binary` (time-invariant)
- UK birth status: `bornuk_dv` from `indresp` -\> `ukborn` (time-invariant)
- Urbanicity: `urban_dv` from `indresp` -\> `urban` (time-varying)
- Highest education level: `hiqual_dv` from `indresp` -\> `edu_qual` (time-invariant)
- De facto marital status: `mastat_dv` from `indresp` -\> `marstat` (time-varying)

```{r}
#| label: demo-init
#| code-summary: Filtering variables
ind_demo <- UKHLS_total %>%
  select(pidp, hidp, wavename, age_dv, sex_dv, doby_dv, ethn_dv, urban_dv, hiqual_dv, mastat_dv)
```

```{r}
#| label: demo-age
#| code-summary: Age
# age - time-varying
table(ind_demo$age_dv, useNA = "ifany")
ind_demo <- ind_demo %>%
  rename(age = age_dv) %>%
  mutate(age = case_when(
    age == -9 ~ NA_real_, # missing
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(age)
    ))
table(ind_demo$age, useNA = "ifany")
```

For sex, I set the following values (male = `1`, female = `2`), and set other values to `NA`. For this purposes of this study, sex is considered time-invariant, so I am taking only the first response.

```{r}
#| label: demo-sex
#| code-summary: Sex
table(ind_demo$sex_dv, useNA = "ifany") 
ind_demo <- ind_demo %>%
  rename(sex = sex_dv) %>%
  arrange(pidp, wavename) %>%
  group_by(pidp) %>%
  mutate(
    sex_clean = case_when(
      sex == -9 ~ NA_real_, # missing
      sex == 0 ~ NA_real_, # inconsistent
      TRUE ~ as.numeric(sex)
    ),
    sex = na.omit(sex_clean)[1]
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-sex_clean)
table(ind_demo$sex, useNA = "ifany")
```

For month/day of birth, we would have needed to request special permission, so I am only including year here in terms of year of birth.

```{r}
#| label: demo-yob
#| code-summary: Year of birth
# year of birth (doby_dv) - time-varying
table(ind_demo$doby_dv, useNA = "ifany") 
ind_demo <- ind_demo %>%
  mutate(doby_dv = case_when(
    doby_dv == -9 ~ NA_real_, # missing
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(doby_dv)
  ))
table(ind_demo$doby_dv, useNA = "ifany")
```

Ethnicity is time-invariant, so I am taking the first available response. I am also creating a new column titled `ethn_binary` because there might be underpowering for conducting subgroup analyses at each ethnic category:

- `0` = White (from British/English/Scottish/Welsh/Northern Irish, Irish, Gypsy or Irish Traveller, any other White background — codes 1–4)
- `1` = all others
- Only `-9` should be present, not any of the other codings, and this will be coded to `NA`

```{r}
#| label: demo-ethnicity
#| code-summary: Ethnicity
# checking OG category breakdown - could see 
table(ind_demo$ethn_dv, useNA = "ifany")
ind_demo <- ind_demo %>%
  rename(ethn = ethn_dv) %>%
  arrange(pidp, wavename) %>%
  group_by(pidp) %>%
  mutate(
    ethn_clean = case_when(
      ethn == -9 ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ as.numeric(ethn)
    ),
    ethn = na.omit(ethn_clean)[1]
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-ethn_clean) %>%
  mutate(ethn_binary = case_when(
    is.na(ethn) ~ NA_real_,
    ethn %in% c(1:4) ~ 0, # white
    TRUE ~ 1 # non-white
  ))
table(ind_demo$ethn, useNA = "ifany")
table(ind_demo$ethn_binary, useNA = "ifany")
```

For the UK-born variable, I am actually retrieving from the `xwavedat` file because the `indresp` `ukborn` variable was a proxy. The retrieved variable is time-invariant, and there is only one answer already present.

```{r}
#| label: demo-ukborn
#| code-summary: UK birth status
# retrieve data from xwavedat file, then link by person
xwavedat <- read.delim("UKDA-6614-tab/tab/ukhls/xwavedat.tab", header = TRUE, sep = "\t", quote = "")
ukborn <- xwavedat %>%
  select(pidp, bornuk_dv)
table(ukborn$bornuk_dv, useNA = "ifany") # 1 = born in UK, 2 = not born in UK, -9 = missing
ukborn <- ukborn %>%
  rename(ukborn = bornuk_dv) %>%
  mutate(ukborn = case_when(
    ukborn == -9 ~ NA_real_, # missing
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(ukborn)
  ))
# merging ukborn back into ind_demo (since it's from a different data source)
ind_demo <- ind_demo %>%
  left_join(ukborn, by = c("pidp"))
table(ind_demo$ukborn, useNA = "ifany")
```

Urbanicity is a time-varying derived variable, with `1` = urban, and `2` = rural.

```{r}
#| label: demo-urban
#| code-summary: Urbanicity
table(ind_demo$urban_dv, useNA = "ifany")
ind_demo <- ind_demo %>%
  rename(urban = urban_dv) %>%
  mutate(urban = case_when(
    urban == -9 ~ NA_real_, # missing
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(urban)
  ))
table(ind_demo$urban, useNA = "ifany")
```

I am retrieving the highest educational qualification ever reported, pulling from `hiqual_dv` in the `indresp` file. Although this could technically vary, variance would be minimal among parents, so we have decided to treat it as time-invariant, with the following categories:

- `1` = degree
- `2` = other higher degree
- `3` = A-level etc.
- `4` = GCSE etc.
- `5` = other
- `9` = none (recoding to `6` to maintain step-wise structure)

For this, we also decided to use a loop to obtain non-`NA` variables since we didn't want missingness at a later wave to affect our ability to obtain information.

```{r}
#| label: demo-edu
#| code-summary: Highest educational level
table(ind_demo$hiqual_dv, useNA = "ifany")
ind_demo <- ind_demo %>%
  rename(edu_qual = hiqual_dv) %>%
  arrange(pidp, wavename) %>%
  group_by(pidp) %>%
  mutate(
    edu_qual_clean = case_when(
      edu_qual %in% c(-9, -8) ~ NA_real_,
      edu_qual == 9 ~ 6, # setting a different number to make it step-wise 
      TRUE ~ as.numeric(edu_qual)
    ),
    edu_qual = if (all(is.na(edu_qual_clean))) NA_real_ else min(edu_qual_clean, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-edu_qual_clean)
table(ind_demo$edu_qual, useNA = "ifany")
```

For time-varying de-facto marital status, I am converting the following USOC grouping:

- `-9` (missing) / `-8` (inapplicable) / `-2` (refusal) / `-1` (don't know)

- `0` (child under 16)

- `1` (single and never married/civil partnership)

- `2` (married)

- `3` (same-sex civil partnership)

- `4` (separated but legally married)

- `5` (divorced)

- `6` (widowed)

- `7` (separated from civil partner)

- `8` (former civil partner)

- `9` (former civil partner now widowed)

- `10` (living as couple)

Into the following:

- `1` = single

- `2` = partnered

- `3` = divorced/separated/widowed

```{r}
#| label: demo-marstat
#| code-summary: De-facto marital status
table(ind_demo$mastat_dv, useNA = "ifany")
ind_demo <- ind_demo %>%
  rename(marstat = mastat_dv) %>%
  mutate(marstat = case_when(
    marstat %in% c(-9, -8, -2, -1) ~ NA_real_, # missing
    marstat %in% c(0, 1) ~ 1,
    marstat %in% c(2, 3, 10) ~ 2,
    marstat %in% c(4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9) ~ 3,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(marstat)
  ))
table(ind_demo$marstat, useNA = "ifany")
```

Now that the demographic data is clean, the variables can be merged back into `UKHLS_analytic`.

```{r}
#| label: demo-merge
#| code-summary: Merging sociodemographics back into analytic dataset
n_before <- nrow(UKHLS_analytic)
UKHLS_analytic <- UKHLS_analytic %>%
  inner_join(ind_demo, by = c("pidp", "hidp", "wavename"))
# this merge should carry variables across without restricting the sample, so any change in row count means the join key has not matched as expected
stopifnot(nrow(UKHLS_analytic) == n_before)
```

## Economic variables

These are covariates including household income, income quintile, and occupation class, as well as deriving equivalised income variables from this. While we had initially controlled for household income and occupation class in analyses, we then realised they could be on the causal pathway. Now, I will still obtain information on these economic variables for descriptive purposes, but I will only use the income quintile for stratification.

The relevant variables include:

- `fihhmnnet1_dv` — total net household income (no deductions), derived net monthly
- `ieqmoecd_dv` — modified OECD equivalence scale
- `jbnssec3_dv` — current NS-SEC occupation class, derived (3 class version)

All variables from this section are considered time-varying.

```{r}
#| label: econ-init
#| code-summary: Retrieving economic data variables
ind_econ <- UKHLS_total %>%
  select(pidp, hidp, wavename, fihhmnnet1_dv, ieqmoecd_dv, jbnssec3_dv)
```

```{r}
#| label: econ-income-inspect
#| code-summary: Inspecting household income variables
# cleaning household vars
# household income
table(is.na(ind_econ$fihhmnnet1_dv))
table(is.na(ind_econ$ieqmoecd_dv))
```

I want to create a composite household income variable, dividing total net monthly income by equivalence scale, and also converting it to a yearly equivalised income, in order to use this as a household equivalised income variable.

This variable uses the following existing variables:

- `fihhmnnet1_dv`: total net household income (no deductions), derived net monthly
- `ieqmoecd_dv`: modified OECD equivalence scale (need to set `-9` to NA first)

```{r}
#| label: econ-equivalised
#| code-summary: Creating equivalised household income variable
ind_econ <- ind_econ %>%
  mutate(equiv_monthly = case_when(
    ieqmoecd_dv > 0 ~ fihhmnnet1_dv / ieqmoecd_dv,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_ # in case of invalid equivalence scale
  )) %>%
  mutate(equiv_yearly = equiv_monthly * 12)
summary(ind_econ$equiv_monthly)
hist(ind_econ$equiv_monthly)
summary(ind_econ$equiv_yearly)
```

```{r}
#| label: econ-merge-income
#| code-summary: Merging 'equiv_monthly' and 'equiv_yearly' into analytic sample
# merging back into analytic sample to then calculate the quintiles/deciles
UKHLS_analytic <- UKHLS_analytic %>%
  left_join(ind_econ %>% select(pidp, hidp, wavename, equiv_monthly, equiv_yearly),
            by = c("pidp", "hidp", "wavename"))
```

I am creating income quintiles and deciles using equiv_yearly income (although note, this will have to be recalculated after imputation since I'll have imputed values to consider anyway).

```{r}
#| label: econ-quintiles
#| code-summary: Creating income quintiles and deciles
UKHLS_analytic <- UKHLS_analytic %>%
  group_by(intyear) %>%
  mutate(
    # quintiles (5ths) - for stratified analyses
    income_quintile = ntile(equiv_yearly, 5),
    # deciles (10ths) - for descriptives
    income_decile = ntile(equiv_yearly, 10)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```

Even though these amounts will change, I still want to check the distributions, and there should be roughly the same numbers in each quintile/decile per year.

```{r}
#| label: econ-check-distribution
#| code-summary: Checking distributions of income quintile and decile per year
table(UKHLS_analytic$income_quintile, UKHLS_analytic$intyear, useNA = "ifany")
table(UKHLS_analytic$income_decile, UKHLS_analytic$intyear, useNA = "ifany")
```

```{r}
#| label: econ-summary-quintile
#| code-summary: Checking summary statistics by quintile
UKHLS_analytic %>%
  filter(!is.na(income_quintile)) %>%
  group_by(income_quintile) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    min_income = min(equiv_yearly, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_income = median(equiv_yearly, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_income = max(equiv_yearly, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

Also, I want to double-check there is no overlap within a year (overlap across years is fine because quintiles are relative to each year's distribution). 2015 is chosen at random.

```{r}
#| label: econ-no-overlap-2015
#| code-summary: Checking overlapping information within the year 2015
UKHLS_analytic %>%
  filter(intyear == 2015) %>%
  filter(!is.na(income_quintile)) %>%
  group_by(income_quintile) %>%
  summarise(
    min_income = min(equiv_yearly, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_income = max(equiv_yearly, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: econ-summary-decile
#| code-summary: Checking summary statistics by decile
UKHLS_analytic %>%
  filter(!is.na(income_decile)) %>%
  group_by(income_decile) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    min_income = min(equiv_yearly, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_income = median(equiv_yearly, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_income = max(equiv_yearly, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

As a secondary sense check, I also go back and checked the distribution of equivalised income.

```{r}
#| label: econ-quantiles
#| code-summary: Checking distribution of equivalised income
# check distribution of equivalised income 
quantile(UKHLS_analytic$equiv_yearly, probs = c(0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.90, 0.95, 0.99), na.rm = TRUE)
```

For occupation class, I use NS-SEC coding, which should be derived. I am including a long-term unemployed category (= `4`) and short-term unemployed category (= `5`). To this end, I may have to code inapplicable as inapplicable, and missing as missing for these variables. Occupation class is coded as time-varying.

The current 3-class occupational category, which is as following:

- `1` = management and professional,
- `2` = intermediate,
- `3` = routine and manual,
- `-8` = inapplicable (not employed)
- `-9` = missing

Now gets grouped now into the following:

- `1` = management and professional,
- `2` = intermediate,
- `3` = routine and manual,
- `4` = long-term unemployed (having responded "inapplicable" to 3 or more waves)
- `5` = short-term unemployed (having responded "inapplicable" to \<3 waves)
- `NA` = missing

```{r}
#| label: econ-occupation
#| code-summary: Creating occupation class categories
table(ind_econ$jbnssec3_dv, useNA = "ifany")
ind_econ <- ind_econ %>%
  rename(oc_current = jbnssec3_dv) %>%
  arrange(pidp, wavename) %>%
  group_by(pidp) %>%
  mutate(
    # clean the variable
    oc_clean = case_when(
      oc_current == -9 ~ NA_real_,  # missing
      oc_current == -8 ~ -8,  # inapplicable (not employed)
      TRUE ~ as.numeric(oc_current)
    ),
    # count consecutive unemployment spells
    is_unemployed = (oc_clean == -8),
    # count length of each unemployment spell
    unemploy_length = sequence(rle(is_unemployed)$lengths),
    # mark as long-term unemployed if 3+ consecutive waves
    is_longterm_unemployed = (is_unemployed & unemploy_length >= 3),
    # final coding
    oc_current = case_when(
      oc_clean > 0 ~ oc_clean,  # Has occupation
      is_longterm_unemployed ~ 4,  # 3+ waves unemployed
      oc_clean == -8 ~ 5,  # Short-term unemployment/not employed
      TRUE ~ NA_real_  # Missing only for -9
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-oc_clean, -is_unemployed, -unemploy_length, -is_longterm_unemployed)
table(ind_econ$oc_current, useNA = "ifany")
```

```{r}
#| label: econ-merge-occupation
#| code-summary: Merging occupation back into analytic sample
UKHLS_analytic <- UKHLS_analytic %>%
  left_join(ind_econ %>% select(pidp, hidp, wavename, oc_current), 
            by = c("pidp", "hidp", "wavename"))
```

## Health variables

The next section section of variable preparation before having the clean dataset is combining all variables from the long-standing health variable section and creating a composite variable for them. As mentioned above, I am no longer including disability as a variable because of high missingness, so I stick to `chron_health` only.

```{r}
#| label: health-init
#| code-summary: Retrieving individual variable names
ind_health <- UKHLS_total %>%
  select(pidp, hidp, wavename, hcond1, hcond2, hcond3, hcond4, hcond5, hcond6, hcond7, hcond8, hcond9, hcond10, hcond11, hcond12, hcond13, hcond14, hcond15, hcond16, hcond18, hcond19, hcond21, hcond23, hcond24, hcond26, hcond27, hcond28, hcond29)
```

`chron_health` is a long-standing health variable indicating the presence or absence of a certain condition. Note that not every one of these will be present across every wave. I have decided against using the `health` variable because it contains "mental impairment, illness or disability" as part of the question, and that could be overlapping with the mental health outcome, so instead, I am a creating composite variable as described above. For this one, I've selected variables relating to physical rather than mental health.

From meeting with Jen Dykxhoorn about this, I figured that for health variables, I will need to use loop/feed-forward function for missing/inapplicable, as once individuals have indicated they have that condition, they are not asked again. Also, not all health variables are present at every wave, so I will need to use most recent wave available.

Legend for checking distribution below: `-9` (missing), `-8` (inapplicable), `-7` (proxy), `-2` (refusal), `-1` (don't know), 0 (not mentioned), 1 (yes mentioned).

```{r}
#| label: health-cond-inspect
#| code-summary: Inspect distribution of each chronic condition
# hcond1 = asthma
table(ind_health$hcond1, useNA = "ifany")
# hcond2 = arthritis
table(ind_health$hcond2, useNA = "ifany")
# hcond3 = congestive heart failure
table(ind_health$hcond3, useNA = "ifany")
# hcond4 = coronary heart disease
table(ind_health$hcond4, useNA = "ifany")
# hcond5 = angina
table(ind_health$hcond5, useNA = "ifany")
# hcond6 = heart attack or myocardial infarction
table(ind_health$hcond6, useNA = "ifany")
# hcond7 = stroke
table(ind_health$hcond7, useNA = "ifany")
# hcond8 = emphysema
table(ind_health$hcond8, useNA = "ifany")
# hcond9 = hyperthyroidism or an over-active thyroid
table(ind_health$hcond9, useNA = "ifany")
# hcond10 = hypothyroidism or an under-active thyroid
table(ind_health$hcond10, useNA = "ifany")
# hcond11 = chronic bronchitis
table(ind_health$hcond11, useNA = "ifany")
# hcond12 = any kind of liver condition
table(ind_health$hcond12, useNA = "ifany")
# hcond13 = cancer or malignancy
table(ind_health$hcond13, useNA = "ifany")
# hcond14 = diabetes
table(ind_health$hcond14, useNA = "ifany")

table(ind_health$hcond15, useNA = "ifany")
# hcond16 = high blood pressure
table(ind_health$hcond16, useNA = "ifany")
# hcond18 = other long-standing/chronic condition
table(ind_health$hcond18, useNA = "ifany")

table(ind_health$hcond19, useNA = "ifany")
# hcond21 = COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease)
table(ind_health$hcond21, useNA = "ifany")
# hcond23 = osteoarthritis
table(ind_health$hcond23, useNA = "ifany")

table(ind_health$hcond24, useNA = "ifany")
```

To actually set up the composite `chron_health` variable, I'm using `data.table` as that specific syntax seems to work faster in this case. This code first involves retrieving the individual condition variables, recoding them.

```{r}
#| label: health-cond-setup
#| code-summary: Retrieving and recoding individual chronic health variables
# retrieve chronic condition variables
# the data table is copied before conversion, because select() shares its column vectors with UKHLS_total and data.table's setorder and := modify in place. without the copy, sorting this table reorders pidp, hidp and wavename inside UKHLS_total while leaving its other columns in the original order, silently detaching every variable from its row
ind_health <- data.table::copy(ind_health)
setDT(ind_health)
setorder(ind_health, pidp, wavename)  # locf fills in row order, so sort explicitly
cond_vars <- c(
  "hcond1","hcond2","hcond3","hcond4","hcond5","hcond6",
  "hcond7","hcond8","hcond9","hcond10","hcond11","hcond12",
  "hcond13","hcond14","hcond15","hcond16","hcond18","hcond19",
  "hcond21","hcond23","hcond24","hcond26","hcond27","hcond28",
  "hcond29"
)
# recoding all condition variables (1=yes, 0=no, else NA)
ind_health[, (cond_vars) := lapply(.SD, function(x) fifelse(x == 1, 1, fifelse(x == 0, 0, NA_real_))), 
           .SDcols = cond_vars]
# forward-filling all observations for each person, just in case the flag variable doesn't capture the previous responses
ind_health[, (cond_vars) := lapply(.SD, function(x) nafill(x, type = "locf")), 
           by = pidp, .SDcols = cond_vars]
```

```{r}
#| label: health-cond-composite
#| code-summary: Creating composite variable
# create composite with proper NA handling
ind_health[, chron_health := {
  has_any_data <- rowSums(!is.na(.SD)) > 0
  has_condition <- rowSums(.SD == 1, na.rm = TRUE) > 0
  fifelse(has_any_data, as.integer(has_condition), NA_integer_)
}, .SDcols = cond_vars]
table(ind_health$chron_health, useNA = "ifany")
```

I then select just the composite variable(s) for ease of use in terms of the clean dataset, since I know I won't be using the individual ones here anymore.

```{r}
#| label: health-composite-select
#| code-summary: Selecting composite variable(s) and merging them back into the dataset
ind_health_composite <- ind_health %>%
  select(pidp, hidp, wavename, chron_health)
n_before <- nrow(UKHLS_analytic)
UKHLS_analytic <- UKHLS_analytic %>%
  inner_join(ind_health_composite, by = c("pidp", "hidp", "wavename"))
stopifnot(nrow(UKHLS_analytic) == n_before)
```

## Weights

In this new version, we are adding weights to the dataset and have planned to conduct main analyses with weights included, and a sensitivity analysis with the weights excluded.

To this end, I will be creating a `xw_weight` variable which takes into account the several cross-sectional weight variables across different waves (see above for delineation.

And then, I will export that variable with the other one (`strata` - sampling strata) for use in the sensitivity analyses.

```{r}
#| label: weights-construction
#| code-summary: Retrieving weight-related variables
# the sample-base suffix follows the documented availability of each weight: "us" covers GPS and EMB in wave 1, "ub" adds BHPS for waves 2-6, "ui" adds IEMB for waves 6-13, and "g2" adds GPS2 from wave 14. wave 6 carries both "ub" and "ui" as the transition wave, and wave 14 carries both "g2" and the main interview weight
# the instrument is the self-completion weight, because the outcomes are drawn from the self-completion questionnaire and the guidance is to take the weight for the lowest instrument in the hierarchy that the analysis uses. from wave 15 there is no longer a distinction between self-completion, proxy and main adult interview, so the main interview weight is used there
# the weight columns are checked against their expected wave blocks first: this is the last extraction from UKHLS_total in the section, so it is the point at which any row reordering introduced upstream would show up
stopifnot(
  UKHLS_total %>%
    mutate(expected = case_when(
      wavename == 1 ~ indscus_xw,
      wavename %in% 2:5 ~ indscub_xw,
      wavename %in% 6:13 ~ indscui_xw,
      wavename == 14 ~ indscg2_xw,
      wavename == 15 ~ inding2_xw
    )) %>%
    summarise(missing = sum(is.na(expected))) %>%
    pull(missing) == 0
)

ind_weights <- UKHLS_total %>%
  select(pidp, hidp, wavename, indscus_xw, indscub_xw, indscui_xw, indscg2_xw,
         inding2_xw, memorig, psu, strata) %>%
  mutate(
    xs_weight = case_when(
      wavename == 1 ~ indscus_xw,
      wavename %in% 2:5 ~ indscub_xw,
      wavename %in% 6:13 ~ indscui_xw,
      wavename == 14 ~ indscg2_xw,
      wavename == 15 ~ inding2_xw
    )
  )

# memorig is carried through so that weight coverage can be checked against the sample each person was originally recruited into
ind_weights_composite <- ind_weights %>%
  select(pidp, hidp, wavename, psu, strata, memorig, xs_weight)
```

```{r}
#| label: weights-merging
#| code-summary: Merging weight variables back into clean dataset
n_before <- nrow(UKHLS_analytic)
UKHLS_analytic <- UKHLS_analytic %>%
  inner_join(ind_weights_composite, by = c("pidp", "hidp", "wavename"))
stopifnot(nrow(UKHLS_analytic) == n_before)
```

```{r}
#| label: weights-inspection
#| code-summary: Inspecting weight coverage in the analytic sample
# a weight of zero is a legitimate value meaning the person is out of scope, and applies to temporary sample members and to households in which nobody holds a longitudinal weight. these are excluded from weighted estimates by design and should stay zero, whereas a missing value would mean the wrong weight variable had been selected
summary(UKHLS_analytic$xs_weight)
hist(UKHLS_analytic$xs_weight)

# coverage by wave
UKHLS_analytic %>%
  group_by(wavename) %>%
  summarise(
    n        = n(),
    missing  = sum(is.na(xs_weight)),
    zero     = sum(xs_weight == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    positive = sum(xs_weight > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_pos  = round(100 * positive / n, 1),
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) %>%
  print(n = 15)

# FLOWCHART: weighted analytic sample, since the weighted models exclude zero-weight observations
UKHLS_analytic %>%
  summarise(
    obs_total       = n(),
    obs_weight_pos  = sum(xs_weight > 0),
    ind_weight_pos  = n_distinct(pidp[xs_weight > 0]),
    obs_weight_zero = sum(xs_weight == 0),
    pct_zero        = round(100 * obs_weight_zero / obs_total, 1)
  )
```
