##### Generating figures

This section generates two DiD plots, following the multi-panel/multi-outcome layouts of the ITS section. First, I run a helper command to calculate the pooled marginal means.

```{r}
#| label: did-figure-helpers
#| code-summary: DiD figure helpers
# covariate means for the DiD marginal means, computed once
did_xbar <- covariate_means(imp_long_classic, adj_cov_formula)

# the four cells: group x period
did_grid <- expand.grid(family_3plus = c(0, 1), did_post_period = c(0, 1))

# axis labels built from the windows so they can't drift out of sync
did_period_labels <- c(
  paste0("Pre-policy\n(",  min(did_pre),  "-", max(did_pre),  ")"),
  paste0("Post-policy\n(", min(did_post), "-", max(did_post), ")")
)

# helper: build marginal means for one outcome
build_did_plot_data <- function(model_list, outcome_name) {
  marginal_means_fits(model_list, did_xbar, did_grid, did_design) %>%
    mutate(
      group = ifelse(family_3plus == 0, "Control (1-2 children)", "Treatment (3+ children)"),
      outcome = outcome_name
    )
}

# helper: one DiD panel
# shared_ylim = NULL leaves the panel free-scaled; zero_line adds a dotted reference at 0 for the standardised version
make_did_panel <- function(plot_data, outcome_label, outcome_ylab,
                           shared_ylim = NULL, zero_line = FALSE) {
  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = as.factor(did_post_period), y = pooled_mean,
                             colour = group, shape = group))
  if (zero_line) {
    p <- p + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey40",
                        linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dotted")
  }
  p <- p +
    # policy line, between the two periods
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1.5, colour = "#D55E00",
               linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_point(size = 3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.3)) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper),
                  width = 0.1, linewidth = 0.8,
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.3)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(
      "Control (1-2 children)"  = "#E69F00",
      "Treatment (3+ children)" = "#0072B2"
    ), labels = c(
      "Control (1-2 children)"  = "1-2 children (control)",
      "Treatment (3+ children)" = "3+ children"
    )) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(
      "Control (1-2 children)"  = 16,
      "Treatment (3+ children)" = 15
    ), labels = c(
      "Control (1-2 children)"  = "1-2 children (control)",
      "Treatment (3+ children)" = "3+ children"
    )) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = did_period_labels) +
    labs(title = outcome_label, x = "", y = outcome_ylab,
         colour = "Group", shape = "Group") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(
      plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
      legend.position  = "none",
      axis.text.x      = element_text(size = 7),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )

  if (!is.null(shared_ylim)) {
    p <- p + coord_cartesian(ylim = shared_ylim)
  } else {
    p <- p + scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 5))
  }
  p
}

# create a dummy plot for the DiD legend, built once and reused by both figures
did_legend_source <- ggplot() +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = 1.5, colour = "Two-child benefit cap\nintroduction (2017)"), linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(x = 1, y = 1, colour = "3+ children"), size = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(x = 1, y = 1, colour = "1-2 children (control)"), size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    name = "",
    values = c("Two-child benefit cap\nintroduction (2017)" = "#D55E00",
               "3+ children" = "#0072B2",
               "1-2 children (control)" = "#E69F00"),
    breaks = c("Two-child benefit cap\nintroduction (2017)", "3+ children", "1-2 children (control)"),
    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(
      shape     = c(NA, 15, 16),
      linetype  = c("dashed", "blank", "blank"),
      linewidth = c(0.8, NA, NA)
    ))
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "center", legend.text = element_text(size = 8))

did_legend_panel <- make_legend_panel(did_legend_source)
```

As above, there is a raw classic DiD plot and standardised version.

```{r}
#| label: build-classic-did-plot-data-raw-outcomes
#| code-summary: Raw classic DiD plot
# un-pooled model lists, in outcomes_raw order
did_adj_model_lists <- list(
  did_GHQ_full_adj,
  did_life_sat_full_adj,
  did_self_health_full_adj,
  did_SF_full_adj,
  did_health_sat_full_adj,
  did_finnow_full_adj,
  did_finfut_full_adj
)

did_plot_data_all <- map(seq_along(outcomes_raw), function(j) {
  build_did_plot_data(did_adj_model_lists[[j]], outcomes_raw[j])
})

did_panels <- pmap(list(did_plot_data_all, outcome_labels, outcome_ylabs),
                   function(dat, label, ylab) make_did_panel(dat, label, ylab))

did_combined <- (did_panels[[1]] | did_panels[[2]] | did_panels[[3]] | did_panels[[4]]) /
  (did_panels[[5]] | did_panels[[6]] | did_panels[[7]] | did_legend_panel) +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "Relative change in parental outcomes pre-post the two-child benefit cap for those with 3+ children compared to 1-2 children",
    subtitle = "Marginal means shown. Higher scores indicate worse outcomes.",
    theme    = theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8)
    )
  )

pdf("output/Classic_DiD_multipanel_20260817.pdf", width = 16, height = 9)
print(did_combined)
dev.off()
```

```{r}
#| label: build-classic-did-plot-data-z-scored-out
#| code-summary: Standardised classic DiD plot
# un-pooled z-score model lists, in outcomes_raw order
did_adj_z_model_lists <- list(
  did_GHQ_full_adj_z,
  did_life_sat_full_adj_z,
  did_self_health_full_adj_z,
  did_SF_full_adj_z,
  did_health_sat_full_adj_z,
  did_finnow_full_adj_z,
  did_finfut_full_adj_z
)

did_plot_data_all_z <- map(seq_along(outcomes_z_names), function(j) {
  build_did_plot_data(did_adj_z_model_lists[[j]], outcomes_z_names[j])
})

# shared symmetric y-axis range, computed from the CI bounds so that coord_cartesian cannot clip an error bar at the panel edge
did_z_all_ci <- c(unlist(map(did_plot_data_all_z, ~ .x$ci_lower)),
                  unlist(map(did_plot_data_all_z, ~ .x$ci_upper)))
did_z_ylim <- c(min(did_z_all_ci, na.rm = TRUE) - 0.05,
                max(did_z_all_ci, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.05)
did_z_ylim <- c(-max(abs(did_z_ylim)), max(abs(did_z_ylim)))

did_panels_z <- pmap(list(did_plot_data_all_z, outcome_labels, outcome_ylabs),
                     function(dat, label, ylab) {
  make_did_panel(dat, label, ylab, shared_ylim = did_z_ylim, zero_line = TRUE)
})

did_combined_z <- (did_panels_z[[1]] | did_panels_z[[2]] | did_panels_z[[3]] | did_panels_z[[4]]) /
  (did_panels_z[[5]] | did_panels_z[[6]] | did_panels_z[[7]] | did_legend_panel) +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "Relative change in parental outcomes pre-post the two-child benefit cap for those with 3+ children compared to 1-2 children",
    subtitle = "Marginal means on standardised scale shown. Higher scores indicate worse outcomes.",
    theme    = theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8)
    )
  )

pdf("output/Classic_DiD_multipanel_zscore_20260817.pdf", width = 16, height = 9)
print(did_combined_z)
dev.off()
```

## Controlled Interupted Time Series (CITS)

Finally, the CITS analyses will have a similar setup to the ITS analyses, except that a for-loop is being used here instead of `lapply()` because of memory capacity. Because of that, grid and covariate means for the figures are also calculated here.

```{r}
#| label: cits-figure-setup
#| code-summary: Grid and covariate means for the CITS fitted lines
# defined before the models because the fitted lines and their confidence bands are computed inside each model chunk, while the individual fits still exist. a pooled mipo carries per-term standard errors but not the covariance matrix, so the linear combinations behind the bands cannot be recovered after rm()
cits_xbar <- covariate_means(imp_long_no2017, adj_cov_formula)

cits_years <- setdiff(sort(unique(imp_long_no2017$intyear)), 2017)
cits_grid <- expand.grid(year = cits_years, family_3plus = c(0, 1)) %>%
  mutate(t = year - 2017, post = as.integer(year > 2017))
```

### Full models

These follow the same patterns as before, with unadjusted (raw), adjusted (raw), and standardised adjusted models.

#### Unadjusted (raw)

```{r}

  rm(data_i, design_i)
}
class(cits_finnow_full_adj_z) <- c("mira", "list")
pooled_cits_finnow_full_adj_z <- mice::pool(cits_finnow_full_adj_z)
cits_finnow_adj_z_lines <- marginal_means_fits(cits_finnow_full_adj_z, cits_xbar, cits_grid, cits_design)
rm(cits_finnow_full_adj_z)
gc()
summary(pooled_cits_finnow_full_adj_z, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90)
```

#### Generating figures

For these figures, I will have the same structure as for all the figures created above, with a raw and standardised version - this is building off of the ITS code used above, just adding structure for the control 1-2 children group.

```{r}
#| label: cits-figure-helpers
#| code-summary: CITS figure helpers
# helper: build pooled observed means for CITS (both groups)
build_cits_plot_data <- function(outcome_var, data_long) {
  data_long %>%
    filter(.imp > 0) %>%
    group_by(.imp, intyear, family_3plus) %>%
    summarise(mean_val = mean(.data[[outcome_var]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(intyear, family_3plus) %>%
    summarise(pooled_mean = mean(mean_val), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(intyear != 2017) %>%
    mutate(
      post  = as.integer(intyear > 2017),
      group = ifelse(family_3plus == 0, "1-2 children (control)", "3+ children")
    )
}

# helper: reshape the stored marginal means into plotting form. the pre and post segments are kept separate so ggplot does not connect a line or band across the 2017 gap
prep_cits_lines <- function(lines) {
  lines %>%
    mutate(group = ifelse(family_3plus == 0, "1-2 children (control)", "3+ children"),
           seg   = interaction(group, post))
}

# helper: one CITS panel. shared_ylim = NULL leaves the panel free-scaled; zero_line adds a dotted reference at 0 for the standardised version
make_cits_panel <- function(plot_data, fitted_lines, outcome_label, outcome_ylab,
                            shared_ylim = NULL, zero_line = FALSE) {
  yr_min <- min(plot_data$intyear)
  yr_max <- max(plot_data$intyear)
  fl <- prep_cits_lines(fitted_lines)

  p <- ggplot()
  if (zero_line) {
    p <- p + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey40",
                        linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dotted")
  }
  p <- p +
    # 90% CI bands, drawn first and lighter than the observed points so the points stay legible on top
    geom_ribbon(data = fl,
                aes(x = year, ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper,
                    fill = group, group = seg),
                alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
    # observed means as transparent dots
    geom_point(data = plot_data,
               aes(x = intyear, y = pooled_mean, colour = group),
               size = 2.5, alpha = 0.3) +
    # fitted trend lines, both groups
    geom_line(data = fl,
              aes(x = year, y = pooled_mean, colour = group, group = seg),
              linewidth = 1.1) +
    # policy line
    geom_vline(xintercept = 2017, colour = "#D55E00",
               linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(
      "1-2 children (control)" = "#E69F00",
      "3+ children"            = "#0072B2"
    )) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(
      "1-2 children (control)" = "#E69F00",
      "3+ children"            = "#0072B2"
    ), guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(yr_min, yr_max, by = 2)) +
    labs(title = outcome_label, x = "", y = outcome_ylab, colour = "Group") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
      legend.position  = "none",
      axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )

  if (!is.null(shared_ylim)) p <- p + coord_cartesian(ylim = shared_ylim)
  p
}

# create a dummy plot for the CITS legend, built once and reused by both figures. the confidence band is represented by a wide semi-transparent line segment, since a ribbon cannot be drawn into a legend key directly
cits_legend_source <- ggplot() +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = 1.5, colour = "Two-child benefit cap\nintroduction (2017)"), linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(x = 1, y = 1, colour = "3+ children"), size = 2.5, alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(x = c(1, 2), y = c(1, 2), colour = "3+ children"), linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(aes(x = 1, y = 1, colour = "1-2 children (control)"), size = 2.5, alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(x = c(1, 2), y = c(1, 2), colour = "1-2 children (control)"), linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_line(aes(x = c(1, 2), y = c(1, 2), colour = "90% confidence band"), linewidth = 6, alpha = 0.15) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    name = "",
    values = c("Two-child benefit cap\nintroduction (2017)" = "#D55E00",
               "3+ children" = "#0072B2",
               "1-2 children (control)" = "#E69F00",
               "90% confidence band" = "grey40"),
    breaks = c("Two-child benefit cap\nintroduction (2017)", "3+ children",
               "1-2 children (control)", "90% confidence band"),
    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(
      shape     = c(NA, 16, 16, NA),
      linetype  = c("dashed", "solid", "solid", "solid"),
      linewidth = c(0.8, 1.1, 1.1, 6),
      alpha     = c(1, 1, 1, 0.15)
    ))
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "center", legend.text = element_text(size = 8))

cits_legend_panel <- make_legend_panel(cits_legend_source)
```

```{r}
#| label: cits-figure-raw
#| code-summary: CITS raw adjusted figure — all 7 outcomes
# fitted lines and confidence bands, computed inside the model chunks, in outcomes_raw order
cits_lines_all <- list(
  cits_GHQ_adj_lines,
  cits_life_sat_adj_lines,
  cits_self_health_adj_lines,
  cits_SF_adj_lines,
  cits_health_sat_adj_lines,
  cits_finnow_adj_lines,
  cits_finfut_adj_lines
)

cits_plot_data_all <- map(outcomes_raw, ~build_cits_plot_data(.x, imp_long_no2017))

cits_panels <- pmap(list(seq_along(outcomes_raw), outcome_labels, outcome_ylabs),
                    function(j, label, ylab) {
  make_cits_panel(cits_plot_data_all[[j]], cits_lines_all[[j]], label, ylab)
})

cits_combined <- (cits_panels[[1]] | cits_panels[[2]] | cits_panels[[3]] | cits_panels[[4]]) /
  (cits_panels[[5]] | cits_panels[[6]] | cits_panels[[7]] | cits_legend_panel) +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "Changes in parental outcomes for those with 3+ children compared to 1-2 children",
    subtitle = "Marginal means shown, with 90% confidence bands. Higher scores indicate worse outcomes.",
    theme    = theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9)
    )
  )

pdf("output/CITS_all_outcomes_multipanel_20260817.pdf", width = 16, height = 9)
print(cits_combined)
dev.off()
```

Now, I additionally implement a standardised version.

```{r}
#| label: cits-figure-zscore
#| code-summary: CITS standardised adjusted figure — all 7 outcomes
# fitted lines and confidence bands, computed inside the model chunks, in outcomes_raw order
cits_lines_all_z <- list(
  cits_GHQ_adj_z_lines,
  cits_life_sat_adj_z_lines,
  cits_self_health_adj_z_lines,
  cits_SF_adj_z_lines,
  cits_health_sat_adj_z_lines,
  cits_finnow_adj_z_lines,
  cits_finfut_adj_z_lines
)

cits_plot_data_all_z <- map(outcomes_z_names, ~build_cits_plot_data(.x, imp_long_no2017))

# shared symmetric y-axis range, computed from the confidence bands as well as the observed means so that coord_cartesian cannot clip a band at the panel edge
cits_z_all_vals <- c(
  unlist(map(cits_plot_data_all_z, ~ .x$pooled_mean)),
  unlist(map(cits_lines_all_z, ~ c(.x$ci_lower, .x$ci_upper)))
)
cits_z_ylim <- c(min(cits_z_all_vals, na.rm = TRUE) - 0.15,
                 max(cits_z_all_vals, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.15)
cits_z_ylim <- c(-max(abs(cits_z_ylim)), max(abs(cits_z_ylim)))

cits_panels_z <- pmap(list(seq_along(outcomes_raw), outcome_labels, outcome_ylabs),
                      function(j, label, ylab) {
  make_cits_panel(cits_plot_data_all_z[[j]], cits_lines_all_z[[j]], label, ylab,
                  shared_ylim = cits_z_ylim, zero_line = TRUE)
})

cits_combined_z <- (cits_panels_z[[1]] | cits_panels_z[[2]] | cits_panels_z[[3]] | cits_panels_z[[4]]) /
  (cits_panels_z[[5]] | cits_panels_z[[6]] | cits_panels_z[[7]] | cits_legend_panel) +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "Changes in parental outcomes for those with 3+ children compared to 1-2 children",
    subtitle = "Marginal means on standardised scale from controlled interrupted time series models shown, with 90% confidence bands. Higher scores indicate worse outcomes.",
    theme    = theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9)
    )
  )

pdf("output/CITS_all_outcomes_multipanel_zscore_20260817.pdf", width = 16, height = 9)
print(cits_combined_z)
dev.off()
```

## Sensitivity analyses

There are a few sensitivity analyses here, for slightly different purposes. There is one to verify whether panel weights are needed for analyses (by checking the full models for each method), and another to verify if there is a potential timing impact of the COVID-19 pandemic by running a falsification test, using 2019 as the "pre" timepoint and 2022 as the "post" timepoint. Finally, as mentioned above, I use propensity score matching to run another DiD analysis on the full post-intervention sample, versus just restricting to the 2023 and onwards sample.

### Analyses excluding panel weights

Because the weights are not designed with representativeness of parents (but rather representativeness of the whole country), we also use a sensitivity analysis for the analyses - using the `svydesign()` with an unweighted model (`weights = ~1`). 

#### ITS 

```{r}
#| label: design-its-ghq-total
#| code-summary: Psychological distress
design_its_GHQ <- lapply(1:imp_its$m, function(i) {
  data_i <- mice::complete(imp_its, i)
  # weights of one give the design-based variance without any weighting of the estimates
  design_i <- svydesign(ids = ~psu, strata = ~strata, weights = ~1, data = data_i, nest = TRUE)
  svyglm(GHQ_total_z ~ time_since_policy + post_policy_month + time_since_policy:post_policy_month + age + sex + ethn_binary + ukborn + urban + edu_qual + marstat + chron_health,
         design = design_i)
})
class(design_its_GHQ) <- c("mira", "list")
pooled_design_its_GHQ <- mice::pool(design_its_GHQ)
summary(pooled_design_its_GHQ, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90)
```

### DiD falsification test

As another sensitivity analysis, and in part to evaluate if the timing of the COVID-19 pandemic could have affected results, we run a falsification test by running a DiD with 2019 and 2022 as our "pre" and "post" timepoints respectively. For this, as done above, we use the seven outcomes of the full standardised adjusted model.

#### Code setup

```{r}
#| label: falsification-setup
#| code-summary: Filtering to the falsification windows
fals_pre  <- 2019
fals_post <- 2022
fals_term <- "family_3plus:fals_post_period"

imp_long_fals <- imp_long_no2017 %>%
  filter(intyear %in% c(fals_pre, fals_post)) %>%
  mutate(fals_post_period = as.integer(intyear %in% fals_post))
imp_fals <- as.mids(imp_long_fals)
```

#### Power analysis

Since the sample is only using two years (2019 and 2022), it's worth recalculating the minimum detectable effects to ascertain to what extent a null result is not due to lack of power.

```{r}
#| label: falsification-power
#| code-summary: Minimum detectable effects for the falsification test
# same construction as power-design-constants, on the falsification windows
# restricted to observations with a positive survey weight, since the analysis models are weighted and a zero-weighted observation contributes nothing to the estimates
d_fals <- imp_long_fals %>%
  filter(.imp > 0, !is.na(fals_post_period), xs_weight > 0)

# cell sizes for the DiD level change, over the falsification window
n_cells_fals <- d_fals %>%
  count(.imp, family_3plus, fals_post_period) %>%
  group_by(family_3plus, fals_post_period) %>%
  summarise(n = mean(n), .groups = "drop")

nn_fals <- function(g, p) n_cells_fals$n[n_cells_fals$family_3plus == g & n_cells_fals$fals_post_period == p]

se_fals <- sqrt(1/nn_fals(1, 0) + 1/nn_fals(1, 1) + 1/nn_fals(0, 0) + 1/nn_fals(0, 1))

# average cluster size within the falsification window
mbar_fals <- mbar(d_fals)

falsification_power <- map_dfr(seq_along(outcomes_raw), function(j) {
  pd <- compute_power_stats(outcomes_raw[j], d_fals)
  p_sd <- sqrt(sum((pd$pooled_n - 1) * pd$pooled_sd^2) / sum(pd$pooled_n - 1))
  # the design effect uses this outcome's own ICC, since the share of variance sitting between primary sampling units differs by outcome
  icc_j <- icc_by_outcome$ICC[j]
  deff_fals <- 1 + (mbar_fals - 1) * icc_j

  data.frame(
    Outcome      = outcome_labels[j],
    Analysis     = "DiD falsification (2019 vs 2022)",
    Estimand     = "Level change",
    Alpha        = 0.10,
    Power        = 0.80,
    N_Treatment  = nn_fals(1, 0) + nn_fals(1, 1),
    N_Control    = nn_fals(0, 0) + nn_fals(0, 1),
    Pooled_SD    = p_sd,
    ICC          = icc_j,
    # unadjusted values treat observations as independent
    MDE_SD_units = z_sum * se_fals,
    MDE_Raw      = z_sum * se_fals * p_sd,
    # adjusted values inflate by sqrt(DEFF) to account for clustering within primary sampling units
    DEFF                  = deff_fals,
    MDE_SD_units_adjusted = z_sum * se_fals * sqrt(deff_fals),
    MDE_Raw_adjusted      = z_sum * se_fals * sqrt(deff_fals) * p_sd
  )
})
falsification_power
```

### Difference-in-differences analysis with propensity score matching (DiD + PSM)

#### Matching procedure

In order to keep the before-and-after groups for 3+ children as similar as possible, we wanted to match each individual from the affected post-policy group to an individual with 1) the same number of children, 3) whose youngest child is the same age.

The DiD+PSM analysis will use 2013-2016 as "pre" and 2018-2025 as "post". This is slightly wider periods in each, in order to account for the full post-intervention sample.

```{r}
#| label: psm-period-setup
#| code-summary: Defining the matching periods
# the matching periods are defined here rather than in section 2 so that they are local to this sensitivity analysis and do not enter the imputation model as a predictor. intyear is already a predictor there, and this is a coarsening of it
# 2017 is excluded because the April cutoff falls mid-year
psm_pre  <- 2013:2016
psm_post <- 2018:2025

imp_long_psm <- imp_long_no2017 %>%
  filter(intyear %in% c(psm_pre, psm_post)) %>%
  mutate(psm_post_period = as.integer(intyear %in% psm_post))
imp_psm <- as.mids(imp_long_psm)
```

```{r}
#| label: psm-matching
#| code-summary: Building the matched mids object
# the mids object is needed for the model loops and the power analysis, so it is created here whether or not the matching itself is rerun
# the survey weight is passed as a sampling weight, so that the propensity model is fitted with respect to the weighted population rather than the responding sample, following the recommended approach for propensity score methods under a complex survey design
imp_long_3plus_23 <- imp_long_psm %>%
  filter(family_3plus == 1)
imp_3plus_23 <- as.mids(imp_long_3plus_23)

#matched_imp_23 <- matchthem(
#   psm_post_period ~ age_youngest_child + n_children_5_under,
#   datasets = imp_3plus_23,
#   approach = "within",
#   method = "optimal",
#   ratio = 1,
#   distance = "glm",
#   s.weights = "xs_weight"
# )

summary(matched_imp_23)
saveRDS(matched_imp_23, "UKHLS_imputation_matched_23_20260817.rds")
#matched_imp_23 <- readRDS("UKHLS_imputation_matched_23_20260817.rds")
```

```{r}
#| label: psm-analysis-data
#| code-summary: Combining matched and control data across imputations
# the matched 3+ sample and the unmatched 1-2 control sample, are stacked across imputations - this is used by the power analysis and the figures, the models rebuild this inside their own loops so that each fit sees a single imputation
# the matching weights are dropped because the matching is one to one without replacement, so every matched unit carries a weight of one and the survey weight is the only weight the outcome models need
psm_analysis_long <- map_dfr(1:imp_3plus_23$m, function(i) {
  matched_data <- MatchIt::match.data(matched_imp_23$models[[i]]) %>%
    select(-weights, -subclass, -distance)
  control_data <- mice::complete(imp_no2017, i) %>%
    filter(family_3plus == 0, intyear %in% c(psm_pre, psm_post))
  bind_rows(matched_data, control_data) %>%
    mutate(psm_post_period = as.integer(intyear %in% psm_post), .imp = i)
})
```

#### Updated power analysis for DiD + PSM (matched sample)

Because there are a different number of individuals included in the 3+ children group (only individuals post-policy and their matched pre-policy counterparts), power calculations need to be rerun with the updated Ns. I do this here below, as well as adding a sheet with the updated results to the existing power analysis Excel sheet (so now, this saves as the most recent version).

```{r}
#| label: psm-power
#| code-summary: Minimum detectable effects for the matched sample
# cell sizes for the DiD level change, averaged across imputations
psm_cells <- psm_analysis_long %>%
  count(.imp, family_3plus, psm_post_period) %>%
  group_by(family_3plus, psm_post_period) %>%
  summarise(n = mean(n), .groups = "drop")

nn_psm <- function(g, p) psm_cells$n[psm_cells$family_3plus == g & psm_cells$psm_post_period == p]

se_psm <- sqrt(1/nn_psm(1, 0) + 1/nn_psm(1, 1) + 1/nn_psm(0, 0) + 1/nn_psm(0, 1))

# average cluster size within the matched sample
mbar_psm <- mbar(psm_analysis_long)

psm_power <- map_dfr(seq_along(outcomes_raw), function(j) {
  pd <- compute_power_stats(outcomes_raw[j], psm_analysis_long)
  p_sd <- sqrt(sum((pd$pooled_n - 1) * pd$pooled_sd^2) / sum(pd$pooled_n - 1))
  # the design effect uses this outcome's own ICC, since the share of variance sitting between primary sampling units differs by outcome
  icc_j <- icc_by_outcome$ICC[j]
  deff_psm <- 1 + (mbar_psm - 1) * icc_j

  data.frame(
    Outcome      = outcome_labels[j],
    Analysis     = "DiD + PSM (matched)",
    Estimand     = "Level change",
    Alpha        = 0.10,
    Power        = 0.80,
    N_Treatment  = nn_psm(1, 0) + nn_psm(1, 1),
    N_Control    = nn_psm(0, 0) + nn_psm(0, 1),
    Pooled_SD    = p_sd,
    ICC          = icc_j,
    # unadjusted values treat observations as independent
    MDE_SD_units = z_sum * se_psm,
    MDE_Raw      = z_sum * se_psm * p_sd,
    # adjusted values inflate by sqrt(DEFF) to account for clustering within primary sampling units
    DEFF                  = deff_psm,
    MDE_SD_units_adjusted = z_sum * se_psm * sqrt(deff_psm),
    MDE_Raw_adjusted      = z_sum * se_psm * sqrt(deff_psm) * p_sd
  )
})
psm_power
```

#### DiD + PSM full models

For all of these full models, this uses the same structure as the models above, where full models (standardised adjusted) are run for each outcome.

As done above, all models are pooled across the 20 imputed matched datasets.

```{r}
  design_i <- svydesign(ids = ~psu, strata = ~strata, weights = ~xs_weight, data = analysis_data, nest = TRUE)
  svyglm(finfut_z ~ family_3plus * psm_post_period + age + sex + ethn_binary + ukborn + urban + edu_qual + marstat + chron_health,
         design = design_i)
})
class(psm_finfut_full_adj_z) <- c("mira", "list")
pooled_psm_finfut_full_adj_z <- mice::pool(psm_finfut_full_adj_z)
summary(pooled_psm_finfut_full_adj_z, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90)
```

##### Generating figures

```{r}
#| label: psm-figure-helpers
#| code-summary: DiD + PSM figure helpers
# design-term values for the marginal means, mapping one grid row to the model's own term names
psm_design <- function(row) {
  g <- row$family_3plus
  p <- row$psm_post_period
  list(family_3plus = g, psm_post_period = p,
       "family_3plus:psm_post_period" = g * p)
}

# covariate means for the PSM marginal means, computed once from the combined matched and control data
psm_xbar <- covariate_means(psm_analysis_long, adj_cov_formula)

# the four cells: group x period
psm_grid <- expand.grid(family_3plus = c(0, 1), psm_post_period = c(0, 1))

# axis labels built from the period definitions so they cannot drift out of sync
psm_period_labels <- c(paste0("Pre-policy\n(",  min(psm_pre),  "-", max(psm_pre),  ")"),
                       paste0("Post-policy\n(", min(psm_post), "-", max(psm_post), ")"))

# helper: build marginal means for one outcome
build_psm_plot_data <- function(model_list, outcome_name) {
  marginal_means_fits(model_list, psm_xbar, psm_grid, psm_design) %>%
    mutate(
      group = ifelse(family_3plus == 0, "Control (1-2 children)", "Treatment (3+ children, matched)"),
      outcome = outcome_name
    )
}

# helper: one PSM panel
# shared_ylim = NULL leaves the panel free-scaled; zero_line adds a dotted reference at 0 for the standardised version
make_psm_panel <- function(plot_data, outcome_label, outcome_ylab,
                           shared_ylim = NULL, zero_line = FALSE) {
  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = as.factor(psm_post_period), y = pooled_mean,
                             colour = group, shape = group))
  if (zero_line) {
    p <- p + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey40",
                        linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dotted")
  }
  p <- p +
    # policy line, between the two periods
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1.5, colour = "#D55E00",
               linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_point(size = 3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.3)) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper),
                  width = 0.1, linewidth = 0.8,
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.3)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(
      "Control (1-2 children)"           = "#E69F00",
      "Treatment (3+ children, matched)" = "#0072B2"
    ), labels = c(
      "Control (1-2 children)"           = "1-2 children (control)",
      "Treatment (3+ children, matched)" = "3+ children (matched)"
    )) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(
      "Control (1-2 children)"           = 16,
      "Treatment (3+ children, matched)" = 15
    ), labels = c(
      "Control (1-2 children)"           = "1-2 children (control)",
      "Treatment (3+ children, matched)" = "3+ children (matched)"
    )) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = psm_period_labels) +
    labs(title = outcome_label, x = "", y = outcome_ylab,
         colour = "Group", shape = "Group") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(
      plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
      legend.position  = "none",
      axis.text.x      = element_text(size = 7),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )

  if (!is.null(shared_ylim)) {
    p <- p + coord_cartesian(ylim = shared_ylim)
  } else {
    p <- p + scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 5))
  }
  p
}

# create a dummy plot for the PSM legend, built once and reused by both figures
psm_legend_source <- ggplot() +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = 1.5, colour = "Two-child benefit cap\nintroduction (2017)"), linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(x = 1, y = 1, colour = "3+ children (matched)"), size = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(x = 1, y = 1, colour = "1-2 children (control)"), size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    name = "",
    values = c("Two-child benefit cap\nintroduction (2017)" = "#D55E00",
               "3+ children (matched)" = "#0072B2",
               "1-2 children (control)" = "#E69F00"),
    breaks = c("Two-child benefit cap\nintroduction (2017)", "3+ children (matched)", "1-2 children (control)"),
    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(
      shape     = c(NA, 15, 16),
      linetype  = c("dashed", "blank", "blank"),
      linewidth = c(0.8, NA, NA)
    ))
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "center", legend.text = element_text(size = 8))

psm_legend_panel <- make_legend_panel(psm_legend_source)
```

```{r}
#| label: psm-figure-zscore
#| code-summary: DiD + PSM standardised adjusted figure — all 7 outcomes
# un-pooled z-score model lists, in outcomes_raw order
psm_adj_z_model_lists <- list(
  psm_GHQ_full_adj_z,
  psm_life_sat_full_adj_z,
  psm_self_health_full_adj_z,
  psm_SF_full_adj_z,
  psm_health_sat_full_adj_z,
  psm_finnow_full_adj_z,
  psm_finfut_full_adj_z
)

psm_plot_data_all_z <- map(seq_along(outcomes_z_names), function(j) {
  build_psm_plot_data(psm_adj_z_model_lists[[j]], outcomes_z_names[j])
})

# shared symmetric y-axis range, computed from the CI bounds so that coord_cartesian cannot clip an error bar at the panel edge
psm_z_all_ci <- c(unlist(map(psm_plot_data_all_z, ~ .x$ci_lower)),
                  unlist(map(psm_plot_data_all_z, ~ .x$ci_upper)))
psm_z_ylim <- c(min(psm_z_all_ci, na.rm = TRUE) - 0.05,
                max(psm_z_all_ci, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.05)
psm_z_ylim <- c(-max(abs(psm_z_ylim)), max(abs(psm_z_ylim)))

psm_panels_z <- pmap(list(psm_plot_data_all_z, outcome_labels, outcome_ylabs),
                     function(dat, label, ylab) {
  make_psm_panel(dat, label, ylab, shared_ylim = psm_z_ylim, zero_line = TRUE)
})

psm_combined_z <- (psm_panels_z[[1]] | psm_panels_z[[2]] | psm_panels_z[[3]] | psm_panels_z[[4]]) /
  (psm_panels_z[[5]] | psm_panels_z[[6]] | psm_panels_z[[7]] | psm_legend_panel) +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "Relative change in parental outcomes pre-post the two-child benefit cap for matched 3+ children families compared to 1-2 children",
    subtitle = "Marginal means on standardised scale shown. Higher scores indicate worse outcomes.",
    theme    = theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8)
    )
  )

pdf("output/DiD_PSM_multipanel_zscore_20260817.pdf", width = 16, height = 9)
print(psm_combined_z)
dev.off()
```
